column1: # The audit_url_limits.py candidates, MEASURED. 2026-10-11.
# The lint reported 101 candidates and said running it was the start of the
# work, not the result, because a URL limit on a ranked pivot is the question
# being asked while one on a scheduled read of a finite collection is a
# discard. This settles which is which for the 42 whose URL is a complete
# literal (no runtime %s to fill), by asking each upstream the same question
# with a tenfold limit and comparing.
# 18 TRUNCATING, 5 COMPLETE, 19 UNREACHABLE from here. A `bigger` value of
# 1000/2000/5000 is this test's own ceiling, not the upstream's total -- the
# real shortfall is at least that large.
# Fixed so far: the three udata catalogues, which share od_udata_collect() in
# collectors/sources/od_shared.inc. It made ONE request while the envelope
# published both next_page and the upstream's own total. Measured after:
#   data.public.lu   20 -> 3,193 stored  (= its declared total)
#   dados.gov.pt     20 -> 20,933
#   data.gov.rs      20 -> 3,527
# 27,653 records from three rows that together stored 60.
# ALL 18 ARE NOW FIXED (2026-10-12), and measured again after. Complete, with
# stored == emitted and no truncation notice:
#   nasa-eonet-events        50 -> 7,208    the whole status=open set, 1 request
#   emsc-moment-tensors      50 -> 48,729   = the service's own full_count
#   ifrc-go-emergencies      50 -> 6,088    = its own count
#   peertube-instance-dir   100 -> 1,785    = its own total
#   stats-ar-datos-series   100 -> 271      = its own count
#   gc-hydrometric          500 -> 3,366 observations -> 955 stations
#   geofon-quakes            50 -> 163      a 7-day window, not a count
#   nrcan-quakes             50 -> 42       likewise (and the host 301'd)
#   openaerialmap-imagery    50 -> 21,437 emitted / 21,291 stored
#   stats-nl-cbs-cpi         20 -> 159,120  = /TypedDataSet/$count exactly
# Bounded and DISCLOSED where the corpus is larger than anything wants:
#   spaceflight-news-api     20 -> 2,000 of 36,457   + 1 truncation notice
#   gc-swob-observations    500 -> 10,000 of 18,950  + 1
#   swisstopo-stac           50 -> 2,000             + 1
#   bdc-stac                 20 -> unmeasurable: data.inpe.br resets the
#     connection from here at any limit, which is the UNREACHABLE verdict its
#     own row (line 159) already carried. It shares stac_collect() with the
#     other three, so it is paged and disclosed the same way, unprobed.
# gc-swob-observations was ALSO a rule-4b defect, found by this pass rather
# than reasoned about: it deduped on `tc_id-value` while keying rows on
# `tc_id-value` OR `stn_nam-value`, so a station with no tc_id passed the
# dedupe every time it reported and collapsed at the sink. 25 of 384 on the
# first run; 0 of 432 once both were the same value.
# dea-stac's fix is visible in the DATES it stores: 2026-10-10..2026-10-11
# after, where before it held 2015-10-22 scenes and only those.
# OpenAerialMap's 146 collapses: CORRECTED 2026-10-12. The first reading was
# "the upstream's own duplicates, nothing to fix", on the measurement that 10
# contiguous pages of 100 hold 6 repeated _ids. That measurement is right and
# the conclusion was wrong: an index that reorders between requests serves one
# record twice and another NOT AT ALL, so each visible duplicate implies a
# silent skip. `order_by=_id&sort=asc` takes it to 0 duplicates per 1,000 and
# the run to 21,437 emitted / 21,437 stored. Velib was the same shape
# (1,519/1,508 -> 1,519/1,519); a `where=stationcode="13022"` query proved the
# dataset holds exactly one record for the code that appeared twice.
# Rule: an offset or page walk against a live dataset needs order_by on the
# row's own id, and a small collision count on such a walk is a SKIP until
# measured otherwise.
# Two were not truncation bugs at all, and no record count could have shown it:
# dea-stac's default order is OLDEST FIRST, so limit=20 stored the twenty
# oldest Sentinel-2 scenes over Africa (2015-10-22) and re-stored those same
# twenty every six hours; and od_stats_nl_cbs read /ODataApi/, which answers
# $skip with HTTP 500 saying skip lives on /ODataFeed/ only.
# STILL UNMEASURED: the ~59 candidates whose URL carries a runtime %s, which
# cannot be fetched as a literal. tools/audit_url_limits.py lists them.

# ---- the SHARED HELPERS, fixed 2026-10-12 after the 18 above ---------------
# Three helpers took one page while the caller's URL hard-coded a tiny size, so
# the same discard was multiplied by every portal behind them. Measured before
# and after, live:
#   od_ckan_collect()         11 CKAN portals, rows=20&sort=id asc
#     ckan-ch-zurich          20 -> 942       = result.count
#     ckan-energydata-info    20 -> 1,191     =
#     ckan-london-datastore   20 -> 1,306     = (+1 notice: it ignores paging)
#     ckan-de-berlin          20 -> 2,627     =
#     ckan-ca-ontario         20 -> 2,964     =
#     ckan-au-nsw             20 -> 17,192 emitted / 17,191 stored
#     ckan-au-qld             20 -> 188,880 emitted / 188,879 stored = its own
#       result.count exactly, 945 pages, CONFIRMED end to end 2026-10-12. It
#       took three attempts and the first two are the lesson: at a 250 ms
#       hostgate gap page 77 answered HTTP 429 and the walk stopped and said
#       so, which is how the pacing was found to be wrong rather than the
#       ceiling. At 1,500 ms the complete read takes 72 minutes with no 429 and
#       no truncation notice. The single collision is one record against
#       188,880 over a 72-minute walk -- a dataset added while it ran.
#     ckan-de-muenchen        503 behind a bot wall at rows=20 as much as 200
#     ckan-open-africa        403 likewise
#   od_ods_catalog_collect()  7 ODS catalogues, limit=20&order_by=dataset_id
#     ods-ca-vancouver        20 -> 200       = total_count
#     ods-be-brussels         20 -> 207       =
#     ods-be-namur            20 -> 295       =
#     ods-ch-basel            20 -> 364       =
#     ods-ch-thurgau          20 -> 458       =
#     ods-fr-rennes           20 -> 672       =
#     ods-fr-toulouse         20 -> 845       =
#   ODS records tier (od_walk_rows_max / pw_walk_max), + order_by on the id:
#     ods-paris-velib        100 -> 1,519     = total_count
#     ods-sncf-stations      100 -> 2,792     =
#     ods-fr-fuel-prices     100 -> 9,814     =
#     ods-public-geonames     20 -> 10,000 of 171,176, disclosed. The ceiling
#       is the UPSTREAM's: ODS refuses offset+limit past 10,000. The complete
#       set is .../exports/json, 111 MB for all 171,176 rows, which needs a
#       streaming parse this collector does not have -- named in the notice as
#       the remedy rather than silently attempted.
#   canada-hydrometric-realtime  500 -> 7,821 in a one-hour window (the whole
#     collection is 19,108,759 observations and it had no window at all). The
#     observation-level twin of gc-hydrometric on the same endpoint.
# NOT changed, and why: od_ods_rte_eco2mix asks for limit=48&order_by=date_heure
# desc -- the newest 48 readings of the French grid mix, which is a recency
# window, not a truncation of a finite collection. eco2mix-national-tr is
# QUARTER-hourly, so 48 readings are 12 hours against a 1,800 s schedule: 24
# runs of overlap, nothing falls between two runs. (An earlier draft of this
# line said "48 half-hours", which was wrong about the resolution; the
# conclusion holds either way, since both are far wider than the interval.)
# opendata.reseaux-energies.fr answers an EMPTY body from this environment, so
# the total_count is unmeasured here and the reasoning above is interval
# arithmetic against the collector's own declared limit, not a live reading.
#   who-gho-indicator       100 -> 14,112  = @odata.count ($top/$skip/$count)
#   openfda-enforcement      100 -> 18,002 = meta.results.total. The note in
#     that file said total "supports skip/limit paging" and nothing used it;
#     limit=1000 is honoured and skip caps at 25,000, which this corpus fits.
#   arcgis-featureserver     100 -> 900    = returnCountOnly. exceededTransfer-
#     Limit was already carried in the properties, unread.
#   bc-mineral-tenure        500 -> 42,234 = numberMatched. WFS 2.0 REFUSES
#     startIndex without sortBy ("Cannot do natural order without a primary
#     key") -- the same hazard the ODS/OAM rows hit as a silent skip, here as
#     a hard 400, which is the better failure.
#   emsc-quakes              300 -> 437 over a 1-day window
#   iceland-quakes           300 -> 22 over a 14-day AOI window
# FDSN answers an empty result set with HTTP 204 AND NO BODY, so a NULL doc
# arrives where an honest empty belongs. fdsn_quakes() used to report that as
# rc=-1: the Iceland AOI held zero events for the last day when this was
# written, so a 1-day window would have marked a working source dead every
# quiet day. 204 is now rc=0, and the AOI window is 14 days because a single
# box does not produce events the way the globe does.
#   fedidb-servers            40 -> 4,320. `links.next` carried the cursor in
#     the same envelope and nothing followed it; walked by hand, 4,320 servers
#     across 109 pages. `limit` above 40 is refused (the API answers an HTML
#     error page), so 40 is the page size rather than a choice.
#   ioda-outage-alerts       16 of a 200 limit on a quiet hour, so it never
#     truncated on an ordinary day and would truncate silently on exactly the
#     day it matters: a 48-hour window measured 200+ per page. `page` is
#     0-BASED and works (pages 0/1/2 open on different alerts), so `page=0` is
#     in the URL and the walk continues only when a page comes back full. A
#     normal run is still one request.
# ---- TRIAGED, no change, with the reason ----------------------------------
# A URL limit is not automatically a discard, and these are the three shapes
# where it is not. Recorded so the next pass does not re-litigate them.
# the limit IS the question (a ranked or keyed search has no complete answer):
#   cloudflare_radar_jp (top origins / top locations), grayhat_buckets,
#   linkedin_jp_search, note_com_profiles, telegram_jp_channels,
#   tabelog_restaurants, here_japan, mapfan_api, fofa_jp, flickr_geo,
#   satellite_imagery ($top with $orderby ContentDate desc on an entity pivot),
#   soc_fediverse mastodon/lemmy trend lists, eight_sansan (keyed, and the
#   host is unreachable from here).
# a RECENCY window whose count is generous against a short schedule, so no
# record falls between two runs (measured intervals in brackets):
#   eni_energinet_co2 [300 s, limit=10 = 50 min of 5-minute readings],
#   eni_energinet_prodex [300 s, limit=200], eni_elia_load [900 s, limit=100
#   desc = ~25 h of quarter-hours], eni_ukpn_live_faults [300 s, limit=100 and
#   total_count measured at 63 — complete], reddit_jp_subs [limit=100 is
#   Reddit's own listing maximum], mastodon_jp_instances [per-instance public
#   timeline], soc_forges GitHub /events and /gists/public [GitHub caps the
#   public event stream at 300 events whatever is asked, so this is a sample by
#   construction], soc_forges GitLab projects [order_by=last_activity_at].
# already paged, the limit being the STRIDE and not the bound:
#   estat_census / estat_crime / estat_education / estat_employment /
#   estat_household / estat_industry / jstat_map — limit=100000 with
#   startPosition walked off RESULT_INF.NEXT_KEY to the end of the table.
# COMPLETE on the 2026-10-11 measurement, nothing to page:
#   sanc_uk_caselaw (3 of 3), soc_bluesky plc.directory export (1,000 of
#   1,000), od_ckan_london_datastore (it ignores paging and answers whole),
#   soc_fediverse /v1/software (72 of 72), lemmy trends (20 of 20).
# UNMEASURABLE FROM HERE, so unchanged on purpose:
#   trickest_cve — `contents/<year>?per_page=100` against api.github.com, which
#   this session's GitHub proxy answers 403 for repositories outside its scope.
#   The contents API is documented to cap a directory listing at 1,000 entries
#   and to ignore pagination parameters, which would make per_page a no-op and
#   the real remedy the git trees API (/git/trees/{sha}?recursive=1) — but that
#   is inference, not a measurement, so no code changed.
